title: Specified ordinary products and binary/triple evaluation composites
statement:
Fix a finite purity coefficient setting $P$ [def-pur-conventions], with its specified finite commutative ring $A$. On each scheme $X$ use $D_X=D(\operatorname{Sh}(X_{\mathrm{proet}},\operatorname{Mod}(A)))$ in the fixed-scalar presentation [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom]. Let $L_f,R_f,L_f\dashv R_f$ be the published ordinary derived pullback, direct image and adjunction [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations], $\mu_f:L_f(F\otimes G)\cong L_fF\otimes L_fG$ the published tensor comparison, and $c_{r,f}:L_{rf}\cong L_rL_f$ the published pullback compositor. Equality transport is transport of these specified functors. Retain the actual ordinary product $\Omega$ of [def-pur-finite-ordinary-product], not its transpose as a replacement definition.

For a cartesian square $rf=tg$ [def-pc-fibre-product], $F,G\in D_B$, $K\in D_X$, $L\in D_Y$, and arbitrary maps $x:L_fF\to K$, $y:L_gG\to L$, define $\rho_{r,t}(F,G;x,y):L_{tg}(F\otimes G)\to L_rK\otimes L_tL$ by splitting tensor with $\mu_{tg}$, factoring the first pullback via the equality $tg=rf$ and $c_{r,f}$ and the second with $c_{t,g}$, then applying $L_rx\otimes L_ty$.

A triple diagram consists of double fibre products $X_{12},X_{23}$ with projections $p_1,p_2,q_2,q_3$, one common triple scheme $T$, and maps $a:T\to X_{12}$, $b:T\to X_{23}$, $c:T\to X_3$, with four cartesian cones $p_1f_1=p_2f_2$, $q_2f_2=q_3f_3$, $a(p_2f_2)=cf_3$, $(ap_1)f_1=b(q_2f_2)$ and equations $bq_2=ap_2$, $bq_3=c$. Its common tensor is $(L_{ap_1}K\otimes L_{ap_2}L)\otimes L_cM$. The left and right external tensor identifications use exactly $\mu_a,\mu_b$, the inverse pullback compositors, these projection equalities, and the inverse tensor associator on the right. The actual iterated products are the two composites of $\Omega$ with these identifications and equality transports. The common counit map is the left-associated tensor of the three pulled-back counits after the specified factorization of $L_v$, $v=a(p_2f_2)$.

More generally, for arbitrary $F_i\in D_B$ and maps $x_i:L_{f_i}F_i\to M_i$, define $\rho_3(F_1,F_2,F_3;x_1,x_2,x_3)$ by the same common factorization followed by $(L_{ap_1}x_1\otimes L_{ap_2}x_2)\otimes L_cx_3$. These are explicit composites of existing operations and isomorphisms, with no chosen mathematical data or proof holes.
